messages:
svc-monitor-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: elevated 5xx and gateway timeouts detected on /v1/generate (edge/gateway) starting 2026-02-12T11:02:16Z. spike to 2.4% error rate, p99 latency > 3s. automated rule: route_errors > 1% for 5m. tagging incident-key=INC-20260212-01

oncall-alex: paging oncall. i'm awake, looking now. can someone post which regions + models?

eng-runtime: checked metrics: spike originates from eu-west-1 and us-west-2. model routing shows lots of fallback to quantized-legacy nodes. KV prefix-cache miss-rate jumped from 0.7% to 14% across prefix-shard-7..10. eviction_rate for prefix-cache pods spiked at 11:00 UTC.

eng-ml: noted a small rollout at 10:50 that changed tokenization cache keys (we added a version suffix to prefix key). could be incompatible with existing cache entries.

support-jamie: Customer impact: Support reported multiple timeouts for customers using batch-generation endpoints; one high-traffic customer (acct: compass-ai) saw ~400 failed requests in 15m, some retries. CS is triaging and will reach out to customer.

sre-lead: assign mitigation steps. first goal: reduce customer-visible 5xx, second: stabilize cache without data-loss.

oncall-alex: ok immediate plan: 1) enable fallback routing to warm-pool models in same region (no cache dependence), 2) temporarily scale down prefetchers to 1 concurrency to stop thrash, 3) increase prefix-cache TTLs to avoid evictions while we debug. i'll run steps 1+2 now.

eng-runtime: running command: ```kubectl -n inference scale deployment/prefetcher --replicas=2``` -> applied. also patching prefetcher config: `PREFETCH_CONCURRENCY=1` for the rollout.

deploy-bot: :rocket: Patch rollout started for deployment/prefetcher (canary 1/3 -> 2/3) by oncall-alex.

svc-monitor-bot: Graph update: after throttle change, 5xx rate dropped to 1.1% within 90s. p95 latency down ~600ms. still above baseline.

eng-ml: confirming the tokenization key change: new key format is `tk_v2:{model}:{prefix_hash}`. older entries are `tk:{model}:{hash}`. mismatch explains misses. we shipped the key format change without a migration.

sre-lead: so cache corruption not in-memory corruption but key-version mismatch causing massive cold reads and prefetch thrash -> eviction storm. good to know. mitigation: 1) revert key generation OR 2) make prefetchers handle both formats. which is faster?

eng-ml: fastest is to make runtime accept both keys (compat layer) plus a background migration to populate v2 from v1. i'll push a tiny patch to check both keys. takes ~10-15m to build and deploy as a canary.

oncall-alex: while that's building, let's keep fallback routing active and increase TTLs. eng-runtime can you bump cache TTLs on prefix-cache pods? command?

eng-runtime: running: ```kubectl -n inference exec deploy/prefix-cache -- sh -c "redis-cli CONFIG SET maxmemory-policy volatile-lru; redis-cli CONFIG SET timeout 0"``` (note: our prefix-cache is a custom in-memory service, this command is illustrative; applying feature flag TTL bump: `PREFIX_CACHE_DEFAULT_TTL=3600` via configmap). applying configmap patch now.

deploy-bot: ConfigMap updated: inference-prefix-cache-config. Rolling restart scheduled for pods with config change.

svc-monitor-bot: After TTL bump+prefetch throttle: 5xx = 0.48% and error volume trending down. gateway timeouts reduced.

support-jamie: CS: notified Compass-AI that we're investigating and put mitigation in place; they saw fewer errors after 11:10 UTC. continuing to monitor.

eng-ml: canary for compatibility-layer built and running. it checks both `tk_v2:` and `tk:` keys, returns first hit. canary pass on two pods. rolling to 20% now. patch: ```diff
- key = f"tk_v2:{model}:{h}"
+ key_v2 = f"tk_v2:{model}:{h}"
+ key_v1 = f"tk:{model}:{h}"
+ val = cache.get(key_v2) or cache.get(key_v1)
```

oncall-alex: good. once compatibility is 100% rolled, we can safely scale prefetchers back up and revert TTL hack. keep fallback routing enabled for another 15m.

eng-runtime: compatibility rolled to 100% at 11:22 UTC. verifying metrics... prefix-cache miss-rate dropping to baseline ~0.9% over 6m. eviction_rate normalized.

svc-monitor-bot: 11:24 UTC snapshot: 5xx = 0.09%, p99 latency back to baseline. incident automated priority -> reduced.

sre-lead: summary for postmortem: cause = tokenization key schema change (v2) introduced without migration. symptom = mass cold reads + prefetcher thrash -> eviction cascade -> elevated 5xx/timeouts due to backend saturation and fallback errors. mitigation = compatibility-layer rollout, prefetch throttle, TTL increase, fallback routing to warm pool.

support-jamie: customer impact note: Compass-AI saw intermittent failures 11:02-11:12 UTC, estimated 10% of their requests failed initially, most recovered after 11:10. CS to follow up with post-incident report.

oncall-zoe: taking next shift. handoff: incident stable, monitoring for regression for 1 hour, postmortem owner: eng-ml (lead). PagerDuty incident INC-20260212-01 remains open until postmortem posted.

oncall-alex: :white_check_mark: closing live mitigation steps. documenting commands and timeline in the incident ticket. thanks everyone.

eng-ml: followups: add automated migration or compatibility guard for key schema changes, add canary guard on tokenization changes, and add metric alert for prefix-key-version-mismatch (ratio of v1 hits to v2 hits).

sre-lead: noted. create follow-up tasks and auto-assign: ENG-ML -> migration + canary, ENG-RUNTIME -> prefetch safety limits + circuit-breaker, SRE -> runbook update for cache-key rollouts.

deploy-bot: Incident ticket INC-20260212-01 updated: mitigation applied, cause identified, next steps assigned.

svc-monitor-bot: Final: 11:30 UTC: incident moved to monitoring.
